AcpCommand.description: One slash command an ACP agent offers in a session.

input_hint.description: What to type after the name, when the command takes input.

AcpCompaction.description:
A compaction of the agent's own conversation (its `compaction_update`,
client protocol 1.41.0), recorded once as it starts and once as it
ends. Clients show it as they show the session's own compaction.

compaction_id.description: The agent's ID for it, the same in its start and its end.

summary.description: The summary the agent kept, when it completed with one.

AcpCompactionState.description:
Where a compaction of the agent's own stands (client protocol
1.41.0). An unknown state reads as `completed`.

oneOf.description: The agent started compacting its conversation.
It failed; a warning `notice` in the same update says why.
It was abandoned, such as by a stop.

AcpConfigOption.description:
One config option an ACP agent offers in a session, such as its model,
mode, or reasoning effort. An agent that offers modes but no mode option
is shown as an option `mode` of category `mode`.

category.description:
The agent's label for what the option is, such as `model`, `mode`,
or `thought_level`.

kind.description:
The option's control: a select (the default, left out) or a boolean
(client protocol 1.23.0).

AcpConfigOptionKind.description:
The control an [`AcpConfigOption`] is (client protocol 1.23.0). An
unknown kind reads as a select, whose `values` a client lists.

oneOf.description: One of `values`.

On or off: `current_value` is `true` or `false`, and `values`
lists both (`true`, named On, and `false`, named Off), so a
client that reads every option as a select can still set it.

AcpContextUsage.description:
How much of its context window the agent's conversation uses, as its
latest `usage_update` reported (client protocol 1.23.0).

size.description: The agent's context window in tokens, when it reported one.

AcpDetachReason.description:
Why a cookie session stopped continuing an ACP session as it
stands (client protocol 1.24.0). An unknown reason reads as
`forked`, which never ends the agent's session.

oneOf.description:
The cookie session is a fork: the ACP session stays its
source's.

The cookie session was reverted to before the end of the ACP
session's conversation: the agent's session holds turns the
cookie session no longer has, and is deleted once the next
turn has branched off it.

AcpDetached.description:
A cookie session's ACP session left behind by a fork or a revert
(client protocol 1.24.0): the next turn of its agent does not resume
it but branches off it at `message_id`, the agent's last message the
cookie session keeps (`session/fork`, else a new session given the
cookie transcript), and the session recorded before is no longer the
cookie session's.

message_id.description:
The ACP `messageId` of the agent's last message the cookie session
keeps; none when it keeps none of the agent's messages.

AcpMessageDirection.description:
Which way an [`AcpSessionMessage`] went (client protocol 1.41.0).
An unknown direction reads as `received`.

oneOf.description: The session got it.
The session sent it.

AcpNotice.description:
An advisory line an ACP agent sent (its `notice` update, or what the
daemon makes of a compaction update), shown where it arrives (client
protocol 1.20.0).

AcpNoticeSeverity.description:
How much an [`AcpNotice`] matters. An unknown severity reads as
`info`.

AcpOptionChoice.description:
A value chosen for one of an ACP agent's config options before its
session exists (client protocol 1.26.0): a draft's model or effort,
applied when the agent's session starts.

AcpSessionMessage.description:
A message between two of the agent's sessions (its `session_message`,
client protocol 1.41.0), such as the task a subagent got or the report
it gave back: shown where it arrives, never sent anywhere.

peer.description:
The other session, as the daemon named it when the message arrived:
a subagent's title or handle, or `parent` for its parent's session.

AcpSessionStart.description:
How the daemon got the ACP session a turn runs in. An unknown way
reads as `new`.

oneOf.description:
`session/new`: the session's first, or the agent could not
resume or load the one it had.
`session/resume` of the session recorded before.

`session/load` of the session recorded before; its replay is
ignored.

`session/fork` of the session a fork or a revert left behind
([`AcpSessionRecord::forked_from`]); client protocol 1.24.0.

A subagent session of the agent's own, which it announced with
`subagent_update` in its parent's session: the cookie session is
a child of the parent's, its runs are the subagent's own work,
and it takes no prompts (client protocol 1.39.0).

AcpSteered.description:
Input the daemon delivered into the agent's running work (an ACP v2
prompt sent during the work; with an ACP v1 agent of an earlier build,
its steering extension), by the events that took it: the
`user_input_submitted` events' sequence numbers and the producer
messages (client protocol 1.20.0).

AcpToolPresentation.description:
A new presentation of one of the agent's own tool calls, whose title,
kind, or arguments arrived after the call started (client protocol
1.20.0). It replaces the call's title, hint, primary argument,
arguments, and preview; its tool identity stays.

AgentMdProject.description: The project an `agent_md_loaded` event's `AGENTS.md` belongs to.

name.description: The project's name when the file was read.

AgentMode.description:
A value this build does not know reads as `internal`: an internal agent,
which is neither runnable as a root nor a delegation target.

selected_suffix_start.description:
Where the run's fallback starts in `fallback_chain`: the run's model
is that entry, and its fallbacks are the entries after it.

action.description: Permission action a tool declares, such as `read`, `bash`, or a runtime's own action.

ApprovalDecisionSource.description: A value this build does not know reads as `system`.

ApprovalFinalOutcome.description: A value this build does not know reads as `cancelled`.

ApprovalFinalization.description:
How an approval ended: the `outcome` of
[`EventPayload::ApprovalFinalized`].

Open: an outcome this build does not know reads as cancelled, so the
operation is not approved.

oneOf.description: A decision by policy, a grant, the reviewer, or the user.

The engine withdrew the approval: the request was cancelled, expired,
or its prepared operation changed or was lost.

rationale.description:
The approval reviewer's one-sentence reason for its verdict, at most
300 characters; absent when it gave none or did not decide (client
protocol 1.28.0).

ApprovalInternalDecisionKind.description: A value this build does not know reads as `ask`: asking the user.

ApprovalReasonCode.description: A value this build does not know reads as `system_error`.

runtime_id.description:
Runtime ID of the tool the request is for; `null` for the base
layer.

tool_call_id.description:
The tool call the request is for, whose `tool_call_started` carries
the call's presentation.

ApprovalResourceSource.description: A value this build does not know reads as `primary_operation`.

ApprovalStep.description:
One step of an approval before its finalization: the `step` of
[`EventPayload::ApprovalStep`].

Open: a step this build does not know changes nothing it reads.

oneOf.description: The internal decision pipeline decided.
The approval waits for the user.

expires_at.description:
When the user's window to answer ends (client protocol 1.28.0):
it starts at the escalation, so the reviewer's time never comes
out of it. The request then carries no `expires_at`, and the
approval's record carries this one. Absent from an earlier
writer, whose request carries the window, and when the window
never ends.

oneOf.description: A client answered for the user.
The same operation was requested too often in a row.

ApprovalTrigger.description: A value this build does not know reads as `permission_policy`.

ApprovalUserDecision.description: A value this build does not know reads as `cancel`.

ArtifactRef.description:
A content-addressed artifact in a session tree's store: a user upload, a
tool attachment, or the full content of a truncated display block.

filename.description: The name the file was attached under, without a directory.

media_type.description: The media type sniffed from the content, such as `image/png`.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the bytes.

BackgroundActor.description:
Who moved a call to the background.

A value this build does not know reads as `model`.

CheckpointNativeWindow.description:
The provider window a summary checkpoint carries beside its summary,
when native compaction succeeded alongside it (client protocol 1.29.0).
A request on the window's provider and model uses it; every other
request uses the summary.

source_through_seq.description: The last event the window covers; it keeps no recent tail apart.

native.description:
The provider window compacted from the same events; absent when
native compaction was not attempted or failed. A reader that
ignores it uses the summary.

oneOf.description:
A provider window alone, which builds before 1.29.0 wrote; read
only. A request that cannot use it compacts the covered events
into a summary first.

recent_from_seq.description:
Where the kept recent tail starts; `null` when the checkpoint keeps
none apart.

action.description: Permission action a tool declares, such as `read`, `bash`, or a runtime's own action.

DelegationStage.description:
How far a delegation got: the `stage` of
[`EventPayload::DelegationProgressed`].

Open: a stage this build does not know changes nothing it reads.

oneOf.description: The child session was published.
A new child run started.

The delegation attached to the already-running run of a resumed
child.
The child waits for a background slot.

DiffAsOf.description:
Whether a diff shows what a call will do (`prepare`) or what it did
(`execute`); the two differ when the file changed in between.

DiffBlock.description: A change to one file, with real file line numbers.

added.description: Lines added by the whole change, omitted hunks included.

hunks.description:
Empty when the change has no line diff, such as a binary or very
large file; `added` and `removed` still count its lines.

removed.description: Lines removed by the whole change, omitted hunks included.

DiffChange.description: How a file changed. An unknown change reads as `modified`.

DiffHunk.description:
A run of changed lines and their context. `old_lines` counts its
`context` and `remove` lines, `new_lines` its `context` and `add` lines.

DisplayBlock.description:
One typed unit of tool presentation.

Text fields allow `\n` and `\t` as their only control characters;
`terminal` segment text also allows SGR colour sequences. Every line
number is a 1-based file line number. `full` is present only on a
truncated block and names its complete content; the `omitted_*` members
count the whole units a cut left out.

oneOf.description: CommonMark.
Consecutive lines of a file.
Output of a process.
Every row has one cell per column.

A checklist of planned steps, such as an ACP agent's plan (client
protocol 1.17.0). Each update replaces the whole list.

DisplayDelta.description: A change to the live display of an executing call.

oneOf.description:
Appends `text` to block `index`, which is a `text` or `terminal`
block. A terminal append extends the last segment when it is of
`stream` (default `stdout`), or starts a new segment. An append to the
index just past the list creates the block: a `terminal` block when
the append names a stream, a `text` block otherwise.
Replaces the whole live list.

ElicitationAction.description:
How a question was answered. An unknown action reads as `Unknown`,
which a client shows as answered.

oneOf.description: The user submitted the form, or agreed to open the URL.
The user said no.
The question was dismissed without an answer.
The user, with `elicitation.respond`.

The daemon, for a session no one attends: one whose permission
mode is `auto_approve_n` (a cron run's default), or a headless
`cookie run`. Always `decline`.
The daemon, as the run was cancelled or ended. Always `cancel`.

The agent reported that the URL's interaction finished
(`elicitation/complete`) before the user answered. Always
`accept`.

The daemon, for a form it cannot show: a required field of a
kind it does not know. Always `decline`.

ElicitationChoice.description:
One choice of a choice field: the value the answer carries and the
label shown.

input.description:
What the field takes. A kind this build does not know cannot be
filled in.

name.description: The member of the answer that carries the field's value.

required.description: An accepted answer must give it a value.

ElicitationForm.description: A form: fields in the order the agent gave them.

ElicitationInput.description: What a field takes, and its default.

oneOf.description: A line of text.

pattern.description:
A regular expression the agent wants the text to match; shown,
not checked.

oneOf.description: One of the choices.
Any number of the choices, in their order.
A number.
A whole number.
Yes or no.

ElicitationValue.description: One field's value in an answer.

cron.description:
The cron job whose fire created this session (client protocol
1.15.0); absent for every other session.

revisions.description: The revisions the session was created against.

oneOf.description: The session was attached to a runtime instance under `name`.

kind.description: Runtime kind the runtime declares, such as `coding` or `global`.

workspace.description: Canonical workspace the runtime reported; absent without one.

oneOf.description: The attachment `name` was removed from the session.

attachment.description:
The coding-runtime attachment whose workspace the files came
from; `global` for a project's `AGENTS.md`, which lives in the
daemon's data directory.

project.description:
The project whose `AGENTS.md` this is, when it is a project's
rather than a workspace's (client protocol 1.8.0). It comes
first in the `AGENTS.md` turn.

oneOf.description:
The memory snapshot the session's model sees from this run on
(`docs/site/specs/memory.md` section 7). An empty snapshot records
that memory is no longer available.

agent.description: The run's agent and its memory; absent in an empty snapshot.

delegated.description:
The snapshot was taken for a delegated run: it holds only the run's
agent's file.

machines.description:
One entry per machine of the session, in the order the session's
attachments first name them.

project.description:
The session's project: its overview whole and an index of its other
memories (client protocol 1.8.0). Only root runs of a session in a
project have it.

rules.description:
A fingerprint of the `memory` rules reaching `global` (the agent's,
then the session overlay's) the snapshot was taken under; a run whose
rules differ takes a new snapshot (client protocol 1.12.0). Absent in
an empty snapshot and in one an earlier daemon took.

taken_at.description:
When the snapshot was taken; the ages it shows are measured to this
time, so equal snapshots render equal text (client protocol
1.14.0). Absent in an empty snapshot and in one an earlier daemon
took.

user.description:
Every valid user category that fits, in name order, including empty
ones.

user_listed.description:
Categories the run's rules ask before reading, listed by URL and
description only, in name order (client protocol 1.12.0).

user_omitted.description: Categories that did not fit, by name, in name order.

writable.description:
The run could see the memory write tools, so the snapshot's text
tells it how to save.

oneOf.description:
A model's memory tool saved, edited, or deleted the memory at `url`
(`docs/site/specs/memory.md` section 16.9.10; client protocol
1.14.0). A transcript shows it as one line, such as `Saved
project://cookie-agent/release`. An audit event: the memory itself
lives outside the session.

A notice about the engine, a plugin, or a runtime: something it
turned off, could not do, or dropped. `detail` is display-only.

count.description: How many occurrences this one record coalesces; absent for one.

kind.description: What a diagnostic reports, as a snake-case label.

source.description: Who a diagnostic is about: `engine:<area>`, `plugin:<name>`, or `runtime:<id>`.

oneOf.description:
Sole durable message body and per-send delivery mode. Acceptance is valid
during an active run without creating a runless UserInputAdmitted.

agent_hop.description:
Internal `send_message` guard metadata: position of this message in
its agent-mail chain (`0` for mail sent by a run that has seen no
agent mail). Never rendered into the agent-visible envelope and
never compared for idempotency. Present exactly on Agent producers'
messages.

idempotency_key.description: Sender-chosen idempotency key scoped to a session and stable producer owner.

retained_output.description:
Engine-retained output the body points the agent at (a background
job's full stdout/stderr). Recording it here keeps the artifacts
alive for later reads; plugins cannot supply it.

oneOf.description:
Run-scoped reference, not a second body or consumption marker. Its event
sequence participates in ModelTurnCommitted.input_through_seq coverage.

Run-scoped reservation of pending admitted messages. The envelope
sequence is the claim token, not proof that provider dispatch occurred.
Releases the claim identified by a ProducerMessagesClaimed envelope.

Append only after committed model input coverage includes the admission.
Recovery repairs missing markers from that commit, never from API selection.
Pending messages are discarded by stable owner identity.

internal_agents.description: One definition per internal agent kind, in kind order.

revisions.description:
The revisions the run was frozen against, present only when they
differ from the latest the log recorded ([`RevisionFold`]).

oneOf.description: `content` carries text parts only.

Input waiting for the running run to complete. The run the engine
then starts with it carries `client_run_id`; a failed, cancelled, or
interrupted run voids every queued input instead.
Its author withdrew the queued input at `queued_seq`.

The engine voided every queued input without starting a run, for
example because the queued run could not start.

A client picked the session's model selection: later runs use it
unless a request names its own, and every client's draft follows it.
The run ended.

Names of the tools sent with this attempt's request, after plugin
rewrites. Recorded only when they differ from the session's previous
record.

The attempt began streaming a text or reasoning part: its first
output, or a switch between the two. The deltas themselves are
live-only; this durably records where in the log, and when, each
streamed part began.
Live-only: delivered as a [`TransientEvent`], never persisted.
Live-only: delivered as a [`TransientEvent`], never persisted.

Live-only: text an internal agent is streaming, delivered as a
[`TransientEvent`] and never persisted. Its terminal internal-agent
event is the durable record.

Live-only: a provider-native compaction call began, delivered as a
[`TransientEvent`] and never persisted.

Live-only: the provider-native compaction call returned, whether or
not it produced a window. A committed checkpoint is the durable record
of a success.

model_error.description:
The model error that ended the attempt (retry, fallback, or
recovery trigger).

base_attempt_id.description:
An earlier attempt of the same run, with the same resolved model,
whose full decision list this attempt's list extends. Absent means
`ordered_decisions` is the full list.

ordered_decisions.description:
The attempt's replay decisions. With `base_attempt_id`, only the
decisions appended after that attempt's list, which is an exact
prefix of this one.

oneOf.description:
The session's automatic runs stopped (`docs/site/specs/held-sessions.md`,
client protocol 1.34.0): nothing starts a run of it on its own, and
external producers and other agents' mail are refused, until the user
resumes it (`session.resume`, or any input the user submits) or its
parent does.

A resume cleared the session's hold: `session.resume`, or its parent
resuming its subagent with mail.

The provider refused a request because a replayed reasoning block is
bound to a conversation prefix that changed since (Anthropic's
thinking-binding check: its tools or system prompt): the reasoning of
every turn committed at or before `through_seq` is no longer replayed
(`docs/site/specs/thinking-replay-recovery.md`, client protocol
1.33.0).

estimated_cost_pico_usd.description: The price stamped at write time; `null` is unpriced.

background.description:
Whether the call's tool supports the background, so a client may
offer to move the call there.

oneOf.description: Live-only: delivered as a [`TransientEvent`], never persisted.

display.description: A change to the call's live display.

cache_strategies.description: One cache strategy per entry of the child's selected suffix.

revisions.description:
The revisions the child was frozen against, present only when
they differ from the latest the log recorded ([`RevisionFold`]).

oneOf.description: A delegation reached a new stage before it finished.

A delegation finished. It is the durable control record and carries
the teaser transcripts render: `short_id` is the child's handle, and
`preview` the report as `[subagent_output]` previews it.

estimated_cost_pico_usd.description: The price stamped at write time; `null` is unpriced.

oneOf.description:
The root session moved into `project`, or out of any project when it
is absent (client protocol 1.8.0). Only root sessions record it; a
delegated session belongs to its root's project.

A subagent of this root session, `child_session_id`, was created with
`attachments` that the root recorded neither as its own nor as
delegated before (client protocol 1.10.0). Only root sessions record
it; `SessionMeta.delegated_attachments` is its fold.

In place of a record of type `omitted_type` that the writer
deliberately did not carry over, at that record's sequence, run, and
time: a fork writes it for each of its source's delegation records,
whose subagents stay the source's.

omitted_type.description: The type of a session event, as a snake-case label.

agent.description: The ACP agent, as the daemon registers it.

agent_info.description: `agentInfo` as the agent sent it, when it did.

cwd.description: The session's working directory on the runtime's machine.

fork.description:
Whether the agent offers `session/fork` (client protocol 1.24.0);
absent in a record an older build wrote.

fork_point.description:
Whether the agent's `session/fork` forks at a message (the JetBrains
AIR fork point), as the daemon found by asking it; absent until it
has, when `acp_session_updated.fork_point` may say later (client
protocol 1.24.0).

forked_from.description:
The agent's session this one was forked from, for `how: forked`
(client protocol 1.24.0).

protocol_version.description: The ACP protocol version the agent answered `initialize` with.

runtime_agent.description: The agent's ID on the runtime.

steering.description:
Whether the agent takes messages into its running work: input sent
to steer reaches the work, else it waits for the agent's next turn
(client protocol 1.20.0). Every ACP v2 agent does; a record of an
earlier build may say otherwise (an ACP v1 agent without the
steering extension).

oneOf.description:
What the ACP agent reported about its session changed: its
commands, its config options, or its plan (client protocol 1.17.0).

compaction.description:
A compaction of the agent's own starting or ending (client protocol
1.41.0; before, a `notice`).

context.description: The agent's context use, when it changed (client protocol 1.23.0).

detached.description:
The ACP session a fork or a revert left behind (client protocol
1.24.0).

fork_point.description:
Whether the agent's `session/fork` forks at a message, found after
the session's record ([`AcpSessionRecord::fork_point`]; client
protocol 1.24.0).

notice.description: A notice of the agent's, shown once where it arrives.

plan.description: The agent's plan, a `plan` display block.

session_message.description:
A message between the agent's sessions (client protocol 1.41.0;
before, a `notice`).

starting_options.description:
The values the session's new ACP sessions start with, on top of the
agent document's `acp.config` (client protocol 1.26.0): what
`session.create`'s `agent_options` chose. Recorded once, as the
session is created.

steered.description: Input delivered into the running turn.

oneOf.description:
An agent of the run asks the user a question: a form or a URL
(client protocol 1.25.0). The run waits for `elicitation_resolved`.

message.description: What the agent asks, and why.

tool_call_id.description: The tool call the question belongs to, when the agent named one.

url.description:
A page to open, such as a sign-in. Accepting means the user agreed
to open it, not that what happens there is done.

oneOf.description:
The question `elicitation_id` was answered (client protocol
1.25.0).

content.description: The form's values, for an accepted form.

reason.description: Why the daemon answered, when it did.

oneOf.description:
The session tree's permission mode became `mode` (client protocol
1.28.0). Only root sessions record it, outside their runs; loading
the tree restores the newest one.

ExtensionMessageRole.description:
The role of a model message. Closed by design: a role is a part of the
model's history every reader must place, so a new one is a breaking
change. Session history stores it too (`message_injected`).

oneOf.description:
The owner run's model, with `variant` in place of its own when set
(client protocol 1.22.0; `base` is the base variant).

FrozenOpenAiPromptCacheTtl.description: A value this build does not know reads as `30m`, the provider default.

GoalReminderIdentity.description:
Pending reminder metadata, NOT a durable send idempotency key.
Coalescing uses the goal ID and revision, independently of the presentation kind.
After consumption another continuation at the same revision uses a fresh send.

GoalReminderKind.description: Whether a reminder introduces the objective or continues previously consumed work.

GoalStatus.description:
A value this build does not know reads as `cancelled`: a cancelled goal,
which allows no lifecycle change.

HeldReason.description: Why a session's automatic runs stopped (`docs/site/specs/held-sessions.md`).

oneOf.description: The user stopped the session's run.

Its runs failed `failures` times in a row, past `[model_retry]
standard_retries`; `error` is the last run's.

InternalAgentOutcome.description:
How an internal agent invocation ended: the `outcome` of
[`EventPayload::InternalAgentFinished`].

Open: an outcome this build does not know reads as interrupted, with no
result.

action.description: Permission action a tool declares, such as `read`, `bash`, or a runtime's own action.

resource.description: Current wildcard grammar: '*' matches any characters, '?' matches one character, and the exact '${workspace_dir}' expression is allowed; controls, globstar, escapes, classes, and every other brace form are forbidden. Runtime deserialization additionally enforces a maximum of 4096 UTF-8 bytes; x-cookie-agent-maxUtf8Bytes records that byte limit because JSON Schema maxLength counts Unicode code points.

runtime.description: The rule's runtime selector, when it has one.

MemoryChangeKind.description:
What a model did to a memory (`docs/site/specs/memory.md` section
16.9.10).

oneOf.description: `memory_write` created or replaced it.
`memory_edit` changed it.
`memory_delete` deleted it.

MemorySnapshotAgent.description: The run's agent and its memory file.

listed.description:
The file, listed by URL and description only, because the run's
rules ask before reading it (client protocol 1.12.0).

memory.description:
The agent's file, whole; absent when it does not exist, is invalid,
or is `omitted`.

omitted.description: The file exists but its rendered text did not fit the snapshot.

max_size.description: The `[memory]` limit of its kind, in bytes.

modified.description: When the memory was last modified.

size.description: The file's size in bytes, frontmatter included.

MemorySnapshotIndexEntry.description:
One line of a memory index: a machine's, a project's, or a memory the
run's rules ask before reading.

max_size.description: The `[memory]` limit of its kind, in bytes.

modified.description: When the memory was last modified.

size.description: The file's size in bytes, frontmatter included.

url.description:
The memory URL, such as `machine://<machine>/<name>` or
`project://<project>/<name>`.

MemorySnapshotMachine.description: One machine of the session and the index of its memories.

attachments.description:
The session's attachments that run on the machine; empty for the
daemon's machine of a session with only `global`.

memories.description: The machine's memories that fit, newest file first.

omitted.description: How many more memories the machine has.

max_size.description: The `[memory]` limit of its kind, in bytes.

modified.description: When the memory was last modified.

size.description: The file's size in bytes, frontmatter included.

MemorySnapshotProject.description: The session's project and what the snapshot holds of its memories.

memories.description: The project's other memories that fit, newest file first.

omitted.description: How many more memories the project has.

overview.description:
`project://<project>/overview`, whole; absent when it is empty,
missing, invalid, or larger than what the snapshot had room for, in
which case `memories` lists it.

project.description: The project's name when the snapshot was taken.

response_body.description: Bounded diagnostic text permitting newlines and tabs.

ModelFinishReason.description:
Why a model turn ended. A reason this build does not know reads as
[`Self::Other`] with its name, and an `other` object's unknown members are
ignored.

PermissionEffect.description:
A value this build does not know reads as `ask`: asking, the effect that
never runs a call unapproved.

PermissionMode.description: A value this build does not know reads as `ask`: asking.

action.description: Permission action a tool declares, such as `read`, `bash`, or a runtime's own action.

resource.description: Current wildcard grammar: '*' matches any characters, '?' matches one character, and the exact '${workspace_dir}' expression is allowed; controls, globstar, escapes, classes, and every other brace form are forbidden. Runtime deserialization additionally enforces a maximum of 4096 UTF-8 bytes; x-cookie-agent-maxUtf8Bytes records that byte limit because JSON Schema maxLength counts Unicode code points.

runtime.description:
Runtime selector (`bash@labpc`): the rule applies only to tools of
runtimes with this runtime ID. Absent, it applies everywhere,
including the base layer.

PersistedModelBinding.description:
A frozen model binding as session history stores it: the identity a
reader needs to attribute and validate records, and the complete binding
as an opaque value.

`frozen` is today's [`FrozenModelBinding`] (descriptor, request defaults,
provider options, credential and setup bindings, static headers). Nothing
decodes it when a log loads; [`Self::decode`] does, best-effort, only
where the engine runs the binding again.

adapter.description:
The protocol adapter the binding speaks, such as
`oven.openai.responses`.

frozen.description: The complete binding, opaque to readers.

resolved.description: The model reference attempts made with this binding record.

selection.description: One exact base or named-variant model selection.

PersistedToolResult.description:
A tool result as sessions store it and clients receive it. `display` is
what clients show, a list of display blocks sharing one 64 KiB budget;
empty means nothing to show. A session log stores the display's text that
repeats `output` as byte ranges of `output` instead of a second copy
(`crate::stored_display`); decoding expands them, so nothing outside the
engine meets them.

additional_messages.description: Emitted model-history messages. Their files share the 256-file limit with attachments.

attachments.description: Direct result files. Together with files in additional_messages, at most 256 are allowed.

background.description:
Present on the result a call committed when it moved to the
background; the daemon alone sets it.

PlanEntryPriority.description: How much a plan step matters. An unknown priority reads as `medium`.

PlanEntryStatus.description: Where a plan step stands. An unknown status reads as `pending`.

capability.description: Permission action a tool declares, such as `read`, `bash`, or a runtime's own action.

PreparedBindingLifetime.description:
A value this build does not know reads as `process_local`: a binding that is
never restart-stable.

PreparedPresentation.description: The presentation a runtime or plugin supplies from prepare.

arguments.description:
The call's arguments; clients fall back to the raw model arguments
when it is empty.

hint.description: What a tool is for, such as `file_edit`.

preview.description: What the call will do, such as a diff as of prepare.

primary_argument.description: Bounded presentation text; byte-capped only, clients sanitize control characters.

ProducerDeliveryMode.description:
Per-send mode. Queue remains accepted-but-deferred during an active run;
steer joins the next safe request without interrupting an in-flight request.

ProducerOwner.description:
Stable identity used with session + idempotency key for durable deduplication.
External identifies a producer outside the daemon, a plugin or a runtime:
the engine derives `source` from the authenticated connection, never from
send parameters, and the sender chooses `name` when it registers. The
connection epoch that authorizes live sends is runtime-only and never part
of this durable owner or the deduplication key.
GoalControl identifies engine-authored lifecycle steering, not a continuation
reminder; its accepted messages survive goal-controller teardown.
Agent identifies an in-tree agent mail sender; the session identity is
engine-derived from the executing tool context, never from model arguments.
Tool identifies the background result of one tool call that ran in the
background; the call identity is engine-derived from the executing tool
context, never from model arguments.
Subagent identifies a delegated session reporting its finished turns to
its parent.
AcpAgent identifies the session's ACP agent starting work on its own
(`docs/site/specs/acp-v2.md` section 6); the engine derives it from the
live ACP session, and its messages are never sent to the agent.
The owner is durable and participates in `(session, owner, key)` dedup.

oneOf.description: A plugin's or a runtime's named producer.

name.description: A producer's label, chosen by its sender at registration.

source.description: Who produces from outside the daemon: `plugin:<name>` or `runtime:<attachment name>`.

oneOf.description: A delegated session reporting a finished turn to its parent.
The session's ACP agent, starting work no prompt of cookie's started.

expected.description: One exact base or named-variant model selection.

found.description: One exact base or named-variant model selection.

adapter_id.description: Wire adapter a model is reached through, such as `anthropic` or `openai-responses`.

selection.description: One exact base or named-variant model selection.

reference.description:
The one stream's artifact, or the named-stream manifest. Absent when
every stream fit inline.

dropped_bytes.description:
Bytes past the capture limit that the artifact does not hold: it keeps
the stream's head up to the limit and its last stretch, with a marker
line between them.

reference.description:
The stream's full content. Absent, with `sha256`, when the stream fit
its preview and the result output already holds all of it.

RunOutcome.description:
How a run ended: the `outcome` of [`EventPayload::RunFinished`].

Open: an outcome this build does not know reads as interrupted, a run
that ended without this build being able to say how.

model.description: One exact base or named-variant model selection.

RuntimeAttachment.description: One runtime a session is attached to.

capability.description: The capability of the runtime the session uses.

name.description: Session-unique attachment name; the tool prefix on collisions.

runtime_id.description: The runtime the capability instance belongs to.

workspace.description: Canonical workspace path the runtime reported; absent without one.

RuntimeRevisions.description:
The revisions of the runtime a session, run, or delegation was frozen
against.

SessionCron.description:
The job a new-session job's run session was started by
(`SessionMeta::cron`).

job_id.description: A cron job's ID: eight lowercase ASCII letters and digits.

attachment.description:
The attachment that contributed a project skill; its grants apply
only to that attachment's tools. Absent for a user skill.

StreamedOutputKind.description: The kind of part a model attempt streams.

TerminalStream.description:
The stream a terminal segment came from. An unknown stream reads as
`stdout`.

ToolBackground.description:
What became of a call that moved to the background: its work goes on and
reports its result later.

job.description: The job the call runs as, present in the `job` state.

ToolBackgroundState.description:
How a backgrounded call's work goes on. An unknown state reads as
`job` without a job: the call is backgrounded and its result arrives
later.

oneOf.description: It runs as background job `job`, which reports its result once.
The work reports itself, as a subagent's turns do.

ToolEmittedContent.description:
One part of a tool-emitted message: `{"text": …}` or `{"file": …}`. Other
members are ignored.

ToolIdentity.description: The tool a call goes to, as the daemon knows it.

name.description: The name its source knows the tool by.

source.description: Absent when the call names no tool the session offers.

ToolPresentation.description:
How clients show a tool call: the prepared presentation and the tool the
daemon resolved.

arguments.description:
The call's arguments; clients fall back to the raw model arguments
when it is empty.

hint.description: What the tool is for, for icons and grouping.

preview.description: What the call will do, such as a diff as of prepare.

primary_argument.description: Bounded presentation text; byte-capped only, clients sanitize control characters.

ToolSource.description: Where a published tool comes from.

oneOf.description: The daemon's base layer.

An ACP agent's own tool, which the agent runs and reports (client
protocol 1.17.0; `docs/site/specs/acp-agents.md` section 6).

runtime_id.description: Runtime ID the grant applies to; `null` for base-layer tools.

UserContent.description: A user's input: a nonempty list of parts.

UserContentPart.description: One part of a user's input.

event.description:
The event's payload under the event contract (`events.md`); an event
type the plugin does not know reads as [`crate::Open::Unknown`].

seq.description:
The event's sequence; a live-only event carries the sequence of the
durable event it follows.
